summary: AWS Marketplace subscription completed but Redwood org provisioning/entitlement delayed (customer stuck on "No active entitlement")
description:
Issue summary
- Customer subscribed to Redwood Inference via AWS Marketplace (SaaS contract). AWS shows subscription as Active, but Redwood Console onboarding blocked: entitlement validation screen shows "No active marketplace entitlement found" and org provisioning cannot complete.

Impact
- Customer cannot create API keys or make first call; procurement-driven onboarding blocked.
- High risk of churn/delay: customer timeline tied to internal security + procurement milestone.

Customer details
- Company: Copperfield Software
- Purchase path: AWS Marketplace (public offer)
- Region expectation: us-east
- Redwood org: existing org created during trial; attempting to link subscription to that org.

Environment
- Redwood: prod (us-east)
- Marketplace: AWS
- Console flow: Marketplace entrypoint (link subscription -> validate entitlement -> provision org limits)

Steps to reproduce (from customer)
1) Subscribe in AWS Marketplace to "Redwood Inference – Hosted API" (contract accepted).
2) Click "Set up your account" which opens Redwood Console.
3) Sign in and select existing org.
4) Console displays error banner: "We couldn’t find an active AWS Marketplace entitlement for this account yet. Try again in a few minutes." Retry did not help after ~45 minutes.

Initial triage notes
- Suspected eventual consistency / propagation delay between AWS subscription activation and Redwood entitlement sync job ingestion.
- Second possibility: subscription tied to different AWS payer/account than the one used for linking (common with consolidated billing), causing entitlement lookup mismatch.

Investigation
- Checked entitlement-sync job metrics (Datadog dashboard: marketplace-entitlements-sync, prod/us-east). Observed elevated sync lag and intermittent AWS Entitlement Service throttling around 18:10–18:40 UTC.
- Queried entitlement verification endpoint (internal) using customer-provided AWS account ID + product code; no entitlement record present in Redwood DB at time of customer attempt.
- Checked logs for entitlement sync worker: multiple retries with backoff; some runs failing due to transient AWS API errors.

Relevant logs (redacted)
- 2026-01-29T18:22:14Z marketplace-sync-worker (prod/us-east) WARN aws_entitlement_query_failed request_id=aws-req-7f3c... error="ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded" backoff_ms=30000
- 2026-01-29T18:29:03Z marketplace-sync-worker INFO sync_cycle_complete fetched=412 upserted=409 duration_ms=128342 lag_minutes=37
- 2026-01-29T18:33:51Z console-backend INFO marketplace_entitlement_check org_id=org_2R... cloud=aws aws_account_id=*** result="not_found" user_id=usr_9M...

Workaround provided to customer (while investigating)
1) Wait 15–30 minutes and retry "Validate entitlement" in Console (AWS propagation can be delayed).
2) Confirm the AWS payer/account ID used for the purchase (in case of consolidated billing). If different from the user’s assumed account, provide payer ID so we can validate against the correct account.
3) Support-triggered manual refresh: we can run an on-demand entitlement sync for the account and re-check (requires AWS account ID + subscription date/time).

Root cause (most likely)
- Entitlement sync job lag due to transient AWS Entitlement Service throttling caused customer’s entitlement to appear in AWS but not yet be ingested/available in Redwood’s entitlement store. Console validation relies on Redwood-side entitlement record; therefore provisioning remained blocked until sync completed.

Resolution
- Ran manual on-demand entitlement sync targeting customer AWS account ID (prod/us-east) and confirmed entitlement record created.
- Customer retried Console validation successfully; subscription linked to existing org and API key creation unblocked.
- Confirmed first successful API request from customer (tokens generated) after linking.

Follow-ups
- Add/verify alerting for sync lag thresholds + throttling spikes (ENG-22116).
- Improve Console error copy to include expected propagation window + consolidated billing guidance (ENG-22112).
- Ensure entitlement verification endpoint supports targeted refresh for support workflows (ENG-22110).

Customer-facing note (what we told them)
- AWS Marketplace subscription activation can take time to propagate to vendor entitlement systems. We manually refreshed their entitlement and confirmed activation; they should be unblocked. If the issue recurs for any additional subscriptions, contact support with AWS payer/account ID and subscription timestamp for immediate refresh.
